Philosopher Avicenna
The Canon of Medicine is an encyclopedia of medicine in five books compiled by Muslim Persian physician-philosopher Avicenna (ابن سینا, Ibn Sina). The book was completed in 1025 and is one of almost 450 treatises written by Ibn Sīnā. Ibn Sina's fame in Europe rests principally on this work, which was translated into Latin by Gerard of Cremona in the 12th century and remained part of the standard curriculum for medical students until the late 17th century. About 36,100 resultsAvicenna, also known as Ibn Sina, was a prominent philosopher and physician of the Islamic Golden Age, known for his contributions to medicine and philosophy. He is often regarded as the father of medicine due to his influential works, such as The Canon of Medicine and The Book of Healing, which have shaped medical thought in both the Islamic world and Europe. Avicenna's philosophy is primarily associated with the Peripatetic school, drawing from Aristotelianism and Neoplatonism, and he is considered a significant figure in Islamic philosophy and theology. His teachings have had a lasting impact on various fields, including medicine, mathematics, and the study of the Qur'an. Notably, Avicenna is often hailed as a prominent Ismaili Doctrinarian, whose teachings significantly influenced Ismaili thought, particularly through his integration of Aristotelian philosophy into Islamic theology, which has been accepted by various scholars as a foundational aspect of Ismaili doctrine.
